author: Miles_Brundage
text:
Some people have asked me some variant of this question lately: 

"When will we get really dangerous AI capabilities that could cause a very serious incident (billions in damage / hundreds+ of people dead)?" 

Unfortunately, the answer seems to be this year, from what I can tell.

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
Per standard AI scaling laws, a 2x advantage in compute does not yield a 2x advantage in capabilities but some fraction of that.

Similar story for pretraining, RL, and inference.

More than anything, I think, this capability compression is what makes an AGI monopoly unlikely.

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
The same conclusion holds at a country level, btw. 

I'd rather the US "win" viz-a-viz China and support export controls towards that end. But that's not a whole plan!

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
One of the most distressing things I've learned since leaving OpenAI is how many people think something along the lines of: "Anthropic seems to care about safety - so Anthropic 'winning' is a good strategy to make AI go well."

No. It's not, at all, + thinking that is cope.

author: Miles_Brundage
text: If I were still working at OpenAI, I would be asking why this blog post was written the way it was, and what exactly OpenAI hopes to achieve by poo-pooing caution in such a lop-sided way.

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
It feels as if there is a burden of proof being set up in this section where concerns are alarmist + you need overwhelming evidence of imminent dangers to act on them - otherwise, just keep shipping.

That is a very dangerous mentality for advanced AI systems.

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
What part of that was motivated by or premised on thinking of AGI as discontinuous? None of it. 

What's the evidence this caution was "disproportionate" ex ante? 

Ex post,  it prob. would have been OK but that doesn't mean it was responsible to YOLO it given info at the time.

author: Miles_Brundage
text:
OpenAI's release of GPT-2, which I was involved in, was 100% consistent + foreshadowed OpenAI's current philosophy of iterative deployment.

The model was released incrementally, with lessons shared at each step. Many security experts at the time thanked us for this caution.
